budget_items.what_was_said: Warrants covering May 6 through May 16, 2025 were reported for the chair to sign; the committee does not vote on warrants, only line-item transfers.
The committee authorized annual funding for student activity accounts at each school, unchanged from prior years.
The Senate bill to study the Chapter 70 formula includes a state appropriation for a consultant to support the commission's work.
The letter to the legislature will note the number of positions and FTEs cut from the district's permanent staff and the share this represents.
The adopted bus fee policy sets annual per-student fees, reduced rates for reduced-lunch status, no fee for free-lunch status, and family caps for multiple children.
The new superintendent's contract includes dues for a national superintendents' association membership.
The finalized contract sets a starting salary, a three-year term, and an annual increase, aligned in length and percentage with the town manager's contract.

decisions.decision: Member questions to central office staff should be copied to the chair so the chair is aware of recurring issues, within open meeting law limits.
Committee will email the town manager and the chairs of the select board and finance committee to gauge interest in a November special town meeting FY27 override.
Superintendent will provide the committee with a level-services FY27/FY28 budget projection incorporating already-settled bus and teacher/para contracts, before the last meeting of the year.
Level-services budget comparisons will exclude positions funded by free cash, since that funding is one-time and outside the regular budget.
A member will contact assistant town manager Jen Warren to ask how other towns have handled/broken out health insurance in departmental budgets, for comparison purposes.
The committee will proceed with the superintendent's contract as originally negotiated and signed, rather than adopt the attorney's later red-lined revisions or renegotiate.

minutes.headline: Committee reorganized, passed a bus fee policy, and moved to seek a fall FY27 override to stop annual staff layoff threats.
minutes.summary: This was the School Committee's reorganization meeting: three new members were sworn in, officers (chair, vice chair, secretary) and all subcommittee/liaison assignments were elected, and several routine annual votes were taken, including adopting the bus transportation fee policy on its third read. Members also discussed pursuing an FY27 override at a fall special town meeting to end recurring spring layoff threats to staff, asked the superintendent for early budget projections, debated how health insurance costs are counted in the school budget, and resolved confusion over the new superintendent's finalized contract.

what_happened.line: The committee decided to reach out to town boards about seeking a fall special town meeting override to end the annual threat of spring staff layoffs.
Three new members were sworn in and the committee elected a chair, vice chair and secretary as part of its annual reorganization.
The committee adopted a new bus transportation fee policy on its third read, setting reduced and waived rates tied to lunch-assistance status.
A member argued the school budget looks larger relative to other town departments because it carries health insurance costs those budgets do not.
The superintendent agreed to deliver a level-services FY27 budget projection, excluding free-cash-funded positions, before the year's last meeting.

why_it_matters: An override, if it reaches a fall town meeting, would ask residents to approve taxes above the levy cap to fund the school budget rather than face layoffs each spring.
The bus fee policy sets what families pay to ride the bus, with reduced or waived fees tied to free/reduced lunch status and a cap for multiple children.
How health insurance is counted changes what any comparison of the school budget's share of town spending shows, without changing what is actually spent.
